16716-the-going-of-the-white-swan.title: The Going Of The White Swan
16716-the-going-of-the-white-swan.creator: Unknown
16716-the-going-of-the-white-swan.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Presently the man shook his head sorrowfully, and covered up the small disfigured frame again, but this time with a tanned skin of the caribou. The flames of the huge wood-fire dashed the walls and floor with a velvety red and black, and the large iron kettle, bought of the Company at Fort Sacrament, puffed out geysers of steam.

arxiv-2206-05234.title: Probing electron-hole weights of an Andreev bound state by transient currents
arxiv-2206-05234.creator: Zhan Cao, Gu Zhang, Hao Zhang, Wan-Xiu He, Chuanchang Zeng, Ke He, Dong E. Liu
arxiv-2206-05234.description: Abstract Andreev bound states (ABSs) are localized quantum states that contain both electron and hole components. They ubiquitously reside in inhomogeneous superconducting systems. Following theoretical analysis, we propose to probe the electron-hole weights of an ABS via a local tunneling measurement that detects the transient current under a steplike pulse bias.

arxiv-2302-01323.title: The impact of frame quantization on the dynamic range of a one-bit image sensor
arxiv-2302-01323.creator: Lucas J. Koerner
arxiv-2302-01323.description: Abstract For a one-bit image sensor, the number of frames captured determines the quantization step size of the binary rate measurement. The discrete values of the binary rate set a maximum measurable intensity. In this note, we consider how this frame quantization impacts the high-end of the dynamic range of a one-bit image sensor.

arxiv-2401-17298.title: Cataclysmic variables around the period-bounce: An eROSITA-enhanced multi-wavelength catalog
arxiv-2401-17298.creator: Daniela Muñoz-Giraldo, Beate Stelzer, Axel Schwope
arxiv-2401-17298.description: Abstract Context. Cataclysmic variables with degenerate donors which have evolved past the period minimum, also known as period-bouncers, are predicted to make up a great portion of the cataclysmic variable population, between 40 % \% and 70 % \% .

arxiv-2505-22570.title: Tensor product formulas for the Bollobás–Riordan and Krushkal polynomials
arxiv-2505-22570.creator: Iain Moffatt and Maya Thompson
arxiv-2505-22570.description: Abstract Brylawski’s tensor product formula expresses the Tutte polynomial of the tensor product of two graphs in terms of Tutte polynomials arising from the tensor factors. Analogous tensor product formulas are known for the ribbon graph polynomial and transition polynomials of graphs embedded in surfaces, as well as for the Bollobás–Riordan polynomial in some special cases.

arxiv-2510-23618.title: Repulsively Bound Hadrons in a ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} Lattice Gauge Theory
arxiv-2510-23618.creator: Sayak Guha Roy, Vaibhav Sharma, Kaidi Xu, Umberto Borla, Jad C. Halimeh, Kaden R. A. Hazzard
arxiv-2510-23618.description: Abstract A paradigmatic model, the ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} lattice gauge theory exhibits confinement mediated by the gauge field that binds pairs of particles into mesons, drawing connections to quantum chromodynamics. In the absence of any additional attractive interactions between particles, mesons are not known to bind in this model.

arxiv-2511-13836.title: Characteristic Decomposition for Relativistic Numerical Simulations: I. Hydrodynamics
arxiv-2511-13836.creator: Saul A. Teukolsky
arxiv-2511-13836.description: Abstract The characteristic decomposition for GRMHD is not known in a form useful for current numerical simulations. This prevents us from using the most accurate known computational methods, such as full-wave Riemann solvers. In this paper, we present a new method of finding decompositions.

pmc-11385708.title: Nitric Oxide Releasing Coatings for the Prevention of Viral and Bacterial Infections
pmc-11385708.creator: Jenny Aveyard, Siobhan Richards, Man Li, Graeme Pitt, Grant L Hughes, Asangaedem Akpan, Riaz Akhtar, Ahmed Kazaili, Raechelle A D’Sa
pmc-11385708.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Healthcare associated infections (HCAI) represent a significant burden worldwide contributing to morbidity and mortality and result in substantial economic consequences equating to billions annually. Although the impacts of HCAI have been felt for many years, the coronavirus pandemic has had a profound effect, escalating rates of HCAI, even with extensive preventative measures such as vaccination, personal protective equipment, and deep cleaning regimes.

pmc-11633140.title: Placental and immune cell DNA methylation reference panel for bulk tissue cell composition estimation in epidemiological studies
pmc-11633140.creator: Kyle A Campbell, Justin A Colacino, John Dou, Dana C Dolinoy, Sung Kyun Park, Rita Loch-Caruso, Vasantha Padmanabhan, Kelly M Bakulski
pmc-11633140.description: To distinguish DNA methylation (DNAm) from cell proportion changes in whole placental villous tissue research, we developed a robust cell type-specific DNAm reference to estimate cell composition. We collated new and existing cell type DNAm profiles quantified via Illumina EPIC or 450k microarrays.

pmc-12875561.title: Bilateral Inguinal Hernia Repair: Laparoscopic Totally Extraperitoneal Versus Open Lichtenstein
pmc-12875561.creator: Mykhaylo O. Yosypenko, Oleg V. Shulyarenko, Hryhorii O. Havrylov
pmc-12875561.description: AimTo compare the outcome of laparoscopic totally extraperitoneal repair versus the open Lichtenstein technique in the treatment of primary bilateral inguinal hernias.Materials and methodsThe study design was comprised of a matched and randomized research: a total of 93 patients were enrolled in the study and operated in clinic “Medikom” from 2015 to 2022.

pmc-13010987.title: From fish to fork: An analysis of the fishmeal feed chain & presence of Anisakid material
pmc-13010987.creator: Faust Schotte, Ganna Saelens, Brecht Devleesschauwer, Sarah Gabriël
pmc-13010987.description: Anisakid nematodes are zoonotic parasites with a global prevalence in marine fish. Live larvae cause gastrointestinal disease in humans after ingestion of raw or undercooked fish. Alternatively, allergic reactions can occur through exposure to allergens. Emerging evidence shows these allergens may transfer from fishmeal to farmed animals and humans, posing potential public health risks.

pmc-13017821.title: Attenuated rightward hemispheric asymmetry in ADHD: structural MRI evidence from a normalized asymmetry index and its association with cognitive performance
pmc-13017821.creator: Metin Çınaroğlu, Eda Yılmazer, Selami Varol Ülker, Sultan Tarlacı
pmc-13017821.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAltered hemispheric asymmetry has been proposed as a potential neurodevelopmental feature of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). However, findings remain inconsistent, and the functional relevance of structural asymmetry patterns is not well established. This study examines volumetric and cortical-thickness asymmetries across cortical and subcortical regions in children and adolescents with ADHD compared to typically developing controls and evaluates their association with objective cognitive performance.MethodsForty participants with ADHD and 30 age- and sex-matched controls underwent high-resolution T1-weighted MRI.

pmc-13546503.title: Qualitative testing of potential modifications to the EQ-HWB EMV2.1 in adults with mobility problems in the United Kingdom
pmc-13546503.creator: Aisha Moolla, Jill Carlton, Tessa Peasgood
pmc-13546503.description: BackgroundThe EQ-Health and Wellbeing (EQ-HWB) is a generic measure assessing the impact of health, social care, and informal caregiving on quality of life. The 9-item short form, the EQ-HWB-9 v1.1 (experimental, 2022), underwent international validation, with subsequent modifications to item wording, response options, layout, and item order resulting in the EQ-HWB EMV2.1 (experimental modified, 2025).

pmc-13591068.title: Fatty Acid Composition of Fixed Oil of Linum strictum and Its Antibiofilm, Anticoagulant, and α‐Amylase Inhibitory Effects–In Vitro and In Silico Study
pmc-13591068.creator: Hayet Edziri, Pooja Bargali, Marwa Melliti, Hasan Aljohi, Mohammad NasserAlkhrayef, Rim Gtari, Marcello Iriti, Ravendra Kumar, Ibrahim O Alanazi
pmc-13591068.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The present study investigated the fatty acid composition of Linum strictum seed oil and evaluated its antibacterial, antibiofilm, anticoagulant, and α‐amylase inhibitory activities. The oil was extracted from commercially obtained seeds and characterized by GC‐FID. Antibacterial activity was determined using the microbroth dilution method, while antibiofilm activity was assessed against multidrug‐resistant strains, including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, methicillin‐resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), and Acinetobacter baumannii.
